categoryNote: Privacy category. Every entry here is a PRIVACY change and is never described as a performance improvement (directive). Evidence rule applied 2026-11-23: E1 entries cite a Microsoft documentation URL for the exact registry value written and its documented function; E0 layers are labelled as such inside the entry. Edition honesty: Microsoft documents diagnostic data 'off' (AllowTelemetry=0) only for Enterprise/Education/Server, and states that on other editions the value is equivalent to 1 - NX13-004 therefore implements the documented edition floor and never writes a placebo 0 on Home/Pro. Ownership boundaries: Start_Track* values (recent files/app tracking under HKCU\...\Explorer\Advanced) belong to NX15 and are never written here; the NX01 ContentDeliveryManager consumer-content family is not re-targeted; NX11-006 owns generic scheduled-task management and NX13-013 owns only the telemetry-task allow-list; cross-device linking is a declared symmetric conflict with NX12-004. Hosts-file blocking is on the rejected list and is not used anywhere in this category.

tweaks.name: Advertising ID disable
tweaks.description: Turns off the Windows advertising ID for apps, at the documented setting and policy layers.
tweaks.objective: Stop apps from using the per-user advertising ID for cross-app ad personalization.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Two documented values, written together exactly as Microsoft documents them in 'Manage connections from Windows operating system components to Microsoft services' section 18.1 General: Enabled=0 (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AdvertisingInfo AND DisabledByGroupPolicy=1 (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\AdvertisingInfo. The same switch is documented as the ADMX policy DisableAdvertisingId ('Turn off the advertising ID', UserProfiles.admx; Policy CSP Privacy maps it to Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\AdvertisingInfo :: DisabledByGroupPolicy). Microsoft's own note is recorded because it matters for honesty: turning the feature off in the UI 'turns off the advertising ID, not just resets it'. Edition honesty: the Policy CSP editions row lists Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT Enterprise (Home is not listed) and the cited article's stated applicability is Enterprise/Server - on Home the values are still written and verified as configuration, but Microsoft does not separately document policy enforcement for Home, so Home enforcement is recorded as documentation-limited rather than claimed. Both values are captured with key- and value-existence flags before mutation; policy-key existence is recorded separately from the real key (Sophia policy-vs-real-key hygiene, r5).
tweaks.defaultState: Advertising ID enabled (Windows default); policy value absent unless a managed environment set it.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms both values are DWord as proposed after apply; one journal verify entry per value.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original value/kind; values that never existed are deleted (policy-off semantics); only-if-ours divergence is reported, never clobbered.

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value (keyExisted, existed, kind, value) journaled before any mutation; policy-key existence recorded separately.

sideEffects: Ads shown by apps are no longer personalized with the advertising ID; the ID is turned off (Microsoft: off, not merely reset).
Home enforcement of the policy layer is documentation-limited (see technicalExplanation); the setting layer is written on every edition.
documentationSource: Live read-only value-family verification on build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Activity history disable
tweaks.description: Disables the activity feed, user-activity publishing and user-activity upload with the three documented OS Policies.
tweaks.objective: Stop Windows from storing and sending the user's activity history.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Three documented device-scope values, written as one set because Microsoft documents them together in section 18.22 Activity History: EnableActivityFeed=0, PublishUserActivities=0, UploadUserActivities=0 (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System (OSPolicy.admx; Policy CSP Privacy documents EnableActivityFeed, PublishUserActivities and UploadUserActivities with the same key). The documented semantics are captured verbatim in the entry design: disabling EnableActivityFeed stops activities being published and disables ActivityFeed cloud sync; PublishUserActivities=0 stops apps and the OS publishing user activities; UploadUserActivities=0 stops upload (deletion of existing activities is independent of this setting, per Microsoft). The Settings toggles ('Store my activity history on this device', 'Send my activity history to Microsoft') are the user-facing equivalent and are not written here: Microsoft documents no per-user registry mapping for them in the cited section, so NEXTRIX deliberately does not guess one. Edition honesty: the CSP editions row lists Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT Enterprise; Home is not listed, so Home enforcement is documentation-limited (values are still journaled and verified as configuration). No host, service or task is touched.
tweaks.defaultState: Activity feed enabled (Windows default); policy values absent unless managed.
tweaks.proposedState: EnableActivityFeed=0, PublishUserActivities=0, UploadUserActivities=0 at the machine policy layer.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms all three values are DWord 0 after apply; gpedit shows the three OS Policies disabled; one journal verify entry per value.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original (values that never existed are removed - policy-off semantics).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value journaled before mutation; policy-key existence recorded separately.

sideEffects: Activity history is no longer stored/roamed/uploaded; previously stored local activities are not deleted (Microsoft: deletion is independent of these policies).
Task View cross-device resume of activities stops working.
documentationSource: Live read-only value-family verification on build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Tailored experiences disable
tweaks.description: Stops Windows from using diagnostic data to tailor tips, ads and recommendations.
tweaks.objective: Remove diagnostic-data-driven personalization of Windows content for the current user.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Written value: DisableTailoredExperiencesWithDiagnosticData=1 (DWord) under HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent. This is the documented User-scope policy 'Do not use diagnostic data for tailored experiences' (CloudContent.admx, User Configuration; Policy CSP Experience AllowTailoredExperiencesWithDiagnosticData). Value-inversion is deliberate and documented, not an error: the CSP switch 0 = not allowed maps to the ADMX value DisableTailoredExperiencesWithDiagnosticData=1, so NEXTRIX writes 1 to disable the feature. Microsoft's own trade-off text is recorded: with the policy set, users 'will still see recommendations, tips and offers, but they may be less relevant'; Cortana customized experiences are out of scope of this policy. Scope honesty: HKCU = current user profile only; other and future profiles keep their own state, and NEXTRIX v1 does not load the Default user hive (coordinator-level design decision, same as NX01 CDM entries). Edition honesty: the CSP editions row lists Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT Enterprise; Home is not listed, so Home enforcement is documentation-limited while the value itself is journaled and verified. Boundary: this entry does not write any ContentDeliveryManager value (NX01 owns that family) - the policy path under Policies\CloudContent is distinct from NX01-003's HKLM consumer-features value.
tweaks.defaultState: Tailored experiences allowed (Windows default); policy value absent.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms the value is DWord 1 after apply; Settings > Privacy & security > General reflects the policy.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the journaled original (policy value removed if it never existed).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue (keyExisted, existed, kind, value) journaled before mutation.

sideEffects: Recommendations, tips and offers still appear but are no longer tailored with diagnostic data (Microsoft's documented wording).
Current user profile only; other profiles unaffected.
documentationSource: Live read-only value-name verification on build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Diagnostic data level (edition-aware documented floor)
tweaks.description: Applies the lowest diagnostics level Microsoft documents for the running edition: 0 on Enterprise/Education/Server, 1 (required) on Home/Pro, plus the documented dump/log limits.
tweaks.objective: Reach the true documentary floor for this edition instead of writing a placebo 0 that Microsoft documents as equivalent to 1.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxDiagnosticDataLevel (src/nxcore/functions/NX13.ps1). Edition resolution: EditionID is read read-only (Get-NxBuildReport, fallback direct CurrentVersion read) and mapped to a documented floor. Microsoft states for AllowTelemetry value 0 ('Security'): 'This value is only applicable to Windows 10 Enterprise, Windows 10 Education, ... Windows Server 2016. Using this setting on other devices is equivalent to setting the value of 1.' NEXTRIX therefore writes AllowTelemetry=0 (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection, DataCollection.admx) only when the edition is Enterprise-family (Enterprise/EnterpriseN/EnterpriseS/EnterpriseG/IoTEnterprise/Server*) or Education, and writes AllowTelemetry=1 on Home/Pro - reporting appliedLevel < requestedLevel with the documented reason, never silently. Unknown edition ids resolve to the conservative floor 1 with an explicit uncertainty note. Both modes add the documented 'Limit Dump Collection' (LimitDumpCollection=1) and 'Limit Diagnostic Log Collection' (LimitDiagnosticLogCollection=1) policies from the same CSP area, which Microsoft documents as limiting dumps to kernel mini/user-mode triage and stopping extra diagnostic-log collection when optional data is configured. Deliberately NOT written: undocumented HKCU DiagTrack 'shadow' values (MaxTelemetryAllowed/ShowedToastAtLevel) that community scripts use - they are not documented values and NEXTRIX does not fabricate policy (r5 policy-vs-real-key hygiene taken to its honest conclusion). No service is touched: DiagTrack is not in NEVER TOUCH by name but NEXTRIX v1 never reconfigures it here; that ownership question belongs to NX11-017 (recorded for the coordinator).
tweaks.defaultState: No policy values: Windows sends required diagnostic data, the user may opt into optional data (Windows default).
tweaks.proposedState: AllowTelemetry=0 + limits (Enterprise/Education/Server) or AllowTelemetry=1 + limits (Home/Pro), machine policy layer.

verify.procedure: The function re-reads every written value via Test-NxConfigurationState and journals one verify entry per value; the result object reports edition, editionFloor, appliedLevel and whether the requested level was fully applied.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original registry value (values that never existed are removed, returning the device to Windows-default policy state).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value before any mutation; the resolved edition and floor are recorded in the function result and journal entries.

sideEffects: On Home/Pro the diagnostics level stops at Required (1): 'diagnostic data off' is not available on these editions by documented configuration (Microsoft equivalence statement), so the entry does not pretend otherwise.
Optional diagnostic data collection is disabled; dump/log detail is limited, which can reduce the detail available when troubleshooting crashes.
Settings > Privacy & security > Diagnostics & feedback shows the policy-managed level and may not be user-editable.

tweaks.name: App permission defaults (location/camera/microphone/contacts/calendar)
tweaks.description: Sets the documented AppPrivacy 'default for all apps' policy per capability, only for the capabilities the owner explicitly selects.
tweaks.objective: Bring the Windows-app permission defaults under an explicit, per-capability, journaled decision - with the current state reported first.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxAppPermissionDefaults (src/nxcore/functions/NX13.ps1). Mechanism: the documented AppPrivacy 'Let Windows apps access <capability>' policies - LetAppsAccessLocation, LetAppsAccessCamera, LetAppsAccessMicrophone, LetAppsAccessContacts, LetAppsAccessCalendar (DWord, 0=user in control, 1=force allow, 2=force deny) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\AppPrivacy (AppPrivacy.admx; Policy CSP Privacy; section 18.2/18.3/18.4/18.8/18.9 of the connections article each document Force Deny as value 2 for the exact value name). Per-item consent is structural: -Permissions is mandatory and only the listed capabilities are written, so the owner decides each capability individually; the function first returns the pre-change report (policy value + the per-user consent-store top-level value) so the decision is informed. Deny writes 2 (force deny); UserControl writes 0 (the documented 'user in control' default). Microsoft's documented consequence is recorded: affected apps must be restarted (or the device restarted) for the change to reach an already-open app. Boundary: per-app override lists (_ForceAllowTheseApps/_ForceDenyTheseApps and the newer desktop-app namespace policies) are NOT written - per-app permission management is NX11-002 territory; the background-apps global value (LetAppsRunInBackground) belongs to NX01-008 and is not touched. The location service itself (and the broader AllowLocation/DisableLocation master switch) is not written: that is a device-level service decision recorded for the owner, not an app-permission default.
tweaks.defaultState: All five capabilities are 'User in control' (policy values absent on a stock machine).
tweaks.proposedState: Selected capabilities force-denied (2) or returned to user control (0) at the AppPrivacy policy layer.

verify.procedure: The function re-reads each written value (Test-NxConfigurationState) and journals a verify entry per capability; the result lists applied/skipped per capability and the pre-change state of each.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the journaled original per value (absent values removed = user in control); the function itself is idempotent and can also be re-run with -Mode UserControl.

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per capability before mutation, plus a read-only consent-store snapshot in the pre-change report.

sideEffects: Force-deny blocks Windows (packaged) apps from the capability for every user of the device and greys the Settings toggle out; meetings, camera apps and location-dependent apps can stop working until the policy is removed.
Already-open apps must be restarted (Microsoft-documented).
Desktop (Win32) apps are governed by the separate documented namespace policies, which this entry does not write.

tweaks.name: App launch tracking policy (non-Start_Track)
tweaks.description: Applies the documented 'Turn off user tracking' policy so Windows stops recording which programs the user runs.
tweaks.objective: Stop app-launch usage tracking at the documented policy layer without touching the NX15-owned Start_Track* values.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Written value: NoInstrumentation=1 (DWord) under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer - the documented User-scope policy 'Turn off user tracking' (StartMenu.admx; Policy CSP ADMX_StartMenu NoInstrumentation), documented as: 'If you enable this policy setting, the system doesn't track the programs that the user runs, and doesn't display frequently used programs in the Start Menu.' Mechanism-owner boundary (wave-1 adjudication): Microsoft documents the Settings toggle 'Let Windows track app launches to improve Start and search results' as Start_TrackProgs=0 under HKCU\...\Explorer\Advanced (connections article 18.1) - the Start_Track* family (Start_TrackProgs, Start_TrackDocs) is owned by NX15, so NEXTRIX-13 does NOT write it, and NX15 must not claim NoInstrumentation. The two are complementary: NoInstrumentation suppresses the tracking system-wide for the user; NX15's per-surface values control the Start/Explorer suggestions UI. If both are applied, the documented 'Turn off user tracking' behaviour also disables personalized menus (Intellimenus is ignored, per Microsoft). Edition honesty: the CSP editions row lists Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT Enterprise; Home is not listed, so Home enforcement is documentation-limited while the value is journaled and verified. HKCU scope = current user only.
tweaks.defaultState: App-launch tracking enabled (Windows default); NoInstrumentation absent.
tweaks.proposedState: NoInstrumentation=1 (HKCU Policies\Explorer) for the current user.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms NoInstrumentation is DWord 1 after apply; a new Explorer session reflects the policy.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the journaled original (value removed if it never existed).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue (keyExisted, existed, kind, value) journaled before mutation.

sideEffects: Windows no longer records program usage for Start/search personalization; frequently-used program lists stop adapting.
Personalized menus are disabled while the policy is set (documented interplay with 'Turn off personalized menus').
Start_TrackProgs/Start_TrackDocs (NX15 territory) are untouched by design.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/manage-connections-from-windows-operating-system-components-to-microsoft-services (18.1 General - Start_TrackProgs documented as the UI equivalent, owned by NX15)

tweaks.name: General consent & ad-personalization toggles
tweaks.description: Sets the remaining documented Settings > Privacy > General toggles: language-list access for locally relevant website content and suggested content in Settings.
tweaks.objective: Complete the General page's documented, non-duplicating consent toggles without re-targeting the advertising-ID or app-tracking entries.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Two documented layers, chosen so no other NX13 entry is duplicated: (1) HttpAcceptLanguageOptOut=1 (DWord) under HKCU\Control Panel\International\User Profile - documented in connections article 18.1 as the registry equivalent of turning off 'Let websites provide locally relevant content by accessing my language list'; (2) DisableWindowsSpotlightOnSettings=1 (DWord) under HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent - the documented User-scope policy 'Turn off Windows Spotlight on Settings' (CloudContent.admx; Policy CSP Experience AllowWindowsSpotlightOnSettings), whose CSP description states explicitly that the user setting is 'Settings -> Privacy -> General -> Show me suggested content in Settings app'. Deliberate exclusions that keep the category non-duplicating: the advertising-ID toggle is NX13-001 (documented Enabled/DisabledByGroupPolicy pair), app-launch tracking is NX13-006, tailored experiences is NX13-003, and the ContentDeliveryManager families belong to NX01 (not written here). Edition honesty: the Experience CSP editions row for AllowWindowsSpotlightOnSettings lists Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT Enterprise - Home is not listed, so Home enforcement is documentation-limited while both values are journaled and verified. HKCU scope = current user only.
tweaks.defaultState: Language-list access allowed and Settings suggestions allowed (Windows default); values absent.
tweaks.proposedState: HttpAcceptLanguageOptOut=1 (HKCU Control Panel\International\User Profile) and DisableWindowsSpotlightOnSettings=1 (HKCU Policies\CloudContent).

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms both values are DWord 1 after apply; Settings > Privacy & security > General reflects the policy-managed toggles.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original (values removed if they never existed - policy-off semantics).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value journaled before mutation.

sideEffects: Websites no longer receive the user's language list for 'locally relevant content'.
Settings app stops showing suggested content (documented Spotlight-on-Settings behaviour).
Current user profile only.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-experience (AllowWindowsSpotlightOnSettings -> DisableWindowsSpotlightOnSettings; CSP text names the Settings > Privacy > General toggle)
Live read-only value verification on build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Feedback frequency configuration
tweaks.description: Sets Windows feedback requests to 'Never' with the documented policy plus the documented per-user SIUF values.
tweaks.objective: Stop Windows from prompting the user for feedback, without touching diagnostic data collection itself.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Two documented layers, matching section 18.16 Feedback & diagnostics exactly: (1) DoNotShowFeedbackNotifications=1 (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection - the documented policy 'Do not show feedback notifications' (FeedbackNotifications.admx; Policy CSP Experience DoNotShowFeedbackNotifications); (2) the documented 'Never' row of the feedback-frequency table: PeriodInNanoSeconds=0 AND NumberOfSIUFInPeriod=0 (DWord) under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Siuf\Rules. Microsoft's note is recorded in the entry design because it bounds the claim: 'Feedback frequency only applies to user-generated feedback, not diagnostic and usage data sent from the device' - this entry therefore changes prompt frequency only; the diagnostic level is NX13-004's mechanism and is not re-targeted here. Per-value journaling captures the pre-change SIUF state (the documented 'Automatically' default is the ABSENCE of both values), so rollback removes them rather than writing a guessed default. Edition honesty: Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT Enterprise are listed for the policy; Home is not listed, so Home enforcement is documentation-limited while all three values are journaled and verified.
tweaks.defaultState: Feedback prompts at the Windows default cadence (SIUF values absent = 'Automatically'); policy absent.
tweaks.proposedState: DoNotShowFeedbackNotifications=1 (policy) and SIUF PeriodInNanoSeconds=0 + NumberOfSIUFInPeriod=0 (per user).

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms all three values are DWord as proposed; Settings > Privacy & security > Feedback shows the policy-managed 'Never' state.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original; SIUF values that never existed are deleted, which Microsoft documents as the 'Automatically' default.

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value journaled before mutation (the absence of the SIUF pair is recorded as the documented default).

sideEffects: Windows stops asking for feedback; the user can still send feedback from Feedback Hub manually.
Diagnostic data collection is unchanged by this entry (NX13-004 owns it).
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/manage-connections-from-windows-operating-system-components-to-microsoft-services (18.16 Feedback & diagnostics, including the Never row)
Live read-only value verification on build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Inking & typing personalization policy
tweaks.description: Stops the inking & typing personalization data store from collecting writing/typing samples for the current user.
tweaks.objective: Disable local inking/typing learning without disabling dictation or online speech.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Written values: RestrictImplicitTextCollection=1 AND RestrictImplicitInkCollection=1 (DWord) under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\InputPersonalization - the two registry settings Microsoft documents in section 18.21 Inking & Typing as the equivalent of turning off 'Improve inking and typing' (Settings > Privacy > Diagnostics & feedback). The documented Group Policy pair ('Improve inking and typing recognition' device policy + 'Turn off automatic learning' user policy) is recorded as the policy-surface analog; NEXTRIX writes the documented registry pair because it is per-user, needs no elevation and is exactly what the Settings toggle changes. Dictation interplay is stated rather than silently decided: online speech recognition is a separate documented switch (AllowInputPersonalization, 18.6 Speech / Privacy CSP), and this entry deliberately does NOT write it - disabling speech services would break dictation and voice typing for users who want those features. Microsoft's additional note is recorded: with diagnostic data at Basic/Security the 'send Microsoft info about how I write' flow is already off, so this entry's local-collection change is complementary, not redundant. Localized evidence check on the authoring machine: both value names were present read-only on build 26300 (2026-11-23).
tweaks.defaultState: Inking & typing personalization enabled (Windows default); restrict values absent.
tweaks.proposedState: RestrictImplicitTextCollection=1 and RestrictImplicitInkCollection=1 for the current user.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms both values are DWord 1 after apply; Settings > Privacy & security > Diagnostics & feedback shows 'Improve inking and typing' off.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original (values removed if they never existed).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value journaled before mutation.

sideEffects: Handwriting-recognition and typing-suggestion personalization stops learning from this user's input; personalized suggestions become less accurate over time.
Dictation and online speech are NOT changed by this entry (separate documented switch, left to the owner).
Current user profile only.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/manage-connections-from-windows-operating-system-components-to-microsoft-services (18.21 Inking & Typing; 18.6 Speech for the dictation boundary)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-privacy (AllowInputPersonalization - recorded as the speech switch, not written)

tweaks.name: Cloud content search preferences
tweaks.description: Disables cloud-content search and web results in Windows Search with the two documented Search policies, with the search-quality trade-off stated.
tweaks.objective: Keep Windows Search local, removing cloud (OneDrive/SharePoint) and web query surfaces.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Two documented values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Search (Search.admx; Policy CSP Search): AllowCloudSearch=0 - 'Allow search and Cortana to search cloud sources like OneDrive and SharePoint' set to not allowed (also documented in connections article 2.1 as a search privacy control); and ConnectedSearchUseWeb=0 - the documented 'Don't search the web or display web results in Search' policy (same key, value name documented by both the CSP and the connections article). Trade-off stated in the entry rather than hidden: web answers/Bing results and Microsoft-account cloud content disappear from Start search and search home; local files, apps and settings results are unaffected, and the ability to search cloud content from within the OneDrive/browser experience itself is outside this switch. Because these are policy values, the corresponding Settings toggles become policy-managed (greyed out) - an intentional, visible consequence. Boundaries: search highlights are NX01-010 (EnableDynamicContentInWSB), indexing scope is NX01-009, and WSearch service configuration is NX11-008 - none of those values is written here, and no service is touched. Edition honesty: the CSP editions row lists Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT Enterprise; Home is not listed, so Home enforcement is documentation-limited while the values are journaled and verified.
tweaks.defaultState: Cloud search and web results allowed (Windows default); policy values absent.
tweaks.proposedState: AllowCloudSearch=0 and ConnectedSearchUseWeb=0 at the machine policy layer.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms both values are DWord 0 after apply; Start search returns local results only and the Settings toggles show as policy-managed.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original (values removed if they never existed - policy-off semantics).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value journaled before mutation; policy-key existence recorded separately.

sideEffects: No web/Bing answers and no OneDrive/SharePoint cloud content in Windows Search; search quality for online content is reduced (stated trade-off).
Search highlights, indexing scope and the WSearch service are untouched (owned by NX01-010, NX01-009 and NX11-008).
documentationSource: Live read-only value-family verification on build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Clipboard history configuration
tweaks.description: Turns off clipboard history with the documented 'Allow Clipboard History' policy plus the Settings toggle value.
tweaks.objective: Stop Windows from retaining a history of copied items for the current user, while copy/paste keeps working.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Two layers, deliberately separated by evidence quality. (1) Documented policy: AllowClipboardHistory=0 (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System - 'Allow Clipboard History' (OSPolicy.admx; Policy CSP Experience AllowClipboardHistory), documented as: history of clipboard contents is not allowed to be stored, change takes effect immediately, and Microsoft's own validation steps note the Settings toggle greys out. (2) Settings value: EnableClipboardHistory=0 (DWord) under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Clipboard - the per-user value behind Settings > System > Clipboard; community-known value, labelled E0 inside this otherwise E1 entry (value name verified present read-only on build 26300, 2026-11-23). Writing both keeps the policy and the visible user preference coherent instead of letting the UI disagree with the enforced state. Scope honesty: clipboard history is per user and local; cross-device clipboard synchronization is a DIFFERENT documented value (AllowCrossDeviceClipboard) owned by NX13-012, and it is not written here. Clipboard content itself, pinned items already stored and third-party clipboard managers are not touched by the policy - the policy prevents new history storage.
tweaks.defaultState: Clipboard history allowed (Windows default); values absent or 1 depending on profile history.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms both values are DWord 0; Win+V shows no history and Settings > System > Clipboard shows the policy-managed off state (Microsoft's documented validation).

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original (policy value removed if it never existed).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per layer journaled before mutation; policy-key existence recorded separately from the per-user key.

sideEffects: Clipboard history (Win+V) retains nothing new; copying and pasting itself still works.
Cross-device clipboard synchronization is a separate switch (NX13-012) and is not changed here.
documentationSource: Live read-only value-name verification of EnableClipboardHistory on build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Cross-device experiences configuration
tweaks.description: Disables phone-PC linking and cross-device clipboard synchronization with two documented policies; declared symmetric conflict with NX12-004.
tweaks.objective: Remove the Windows-side cross-device linking and clipboard-roaming surfaces without deleting any app.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Two documented values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System: (1) EnableMmx=0 - the documented 'Phone-PC linking on this device' policy (GroupPolicy.admx; Policy CSP Connectivity AllowPhonePCLinking; Microsoft states that when disabled the device 'isn't allowed to be linked to Phones, will remove itself from the device list of any linked Phones, and can't participate in Continue on PC experiences', effective after reboot); (2) AllowCrossDeviceClipboard=0 - documented 'Allow Clipboard synchronization across devices' (OSPolicy.admx; Policy CSP Privacy; connections article section 30 Cloud Clipboard), documented as preventing clipboard contents being synchronized across devices using the same Microsoft account/Entra account. Legacy spelling recorded but not written: section 18.1 of the connections article documents EnableCdp for the same 'continue experiences' feature; current Windows 11 documentation (Policy CSP Connectivity) maps the policy to EnableMmx, so only the current documented value is written - writing both would be guesswork about which the OS prefers. Deliberate restraint: AllowConnectedDevices=0 (Connectivity CSP) would disable the whole Connected Devices Platform and is NOT written - CDPSvc/CDPUserSvc are on the never-touch service list and many unrelated features depend on CDP. Symmetric conflict declared with NX12-004 (Phone Link removal): removing the Phone Link app and disabling phone-PC linking attack the same feature from two directions, so selecting both is redundant and NX12 must declare this ID back (catalogue line 'Conflict NX13-012 cross-device set'). Also differentiated from NX13-011: clipboard HISTORY (AllowClipboardHistory) is not written here; this entry owns cross-device clipboard ROAMING.
tweaks.defaultState: Phone-PC linking and cross-device clipboard allowed (Windows default); policy values absent.
tweaks.proposedState: EnableMmx=0 and AllowCrossDeviceClipboard=0 at the machine policy layer.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms both values are DWord 0; after the documented reboot the Phones section is unavailable and clipboard sync stops across devices.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original (values removed if they never existed); a linked phone must be re-linked by the user, which Microsoft documents as a consequence of the feature's own state machine rather than something NEXTRIX can restore.

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value journaled before mutation; policy-key existence recorded separately.

sideEffects: No phone-PC linking / Continue-on-PC experiences; previously linked phones are removed from the device list (Microsoft-documented) and must be re-linked after rollback.
Clipboard items no longer roam to other devices of the same account.
Conflicts with NX12-004 Phone Link removal - both reach the same feature; choose one.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/manage-connections-from-windows-operating-system-components-to-microsoft-services (18.1 General EnableCdp legacy spelling; 30 Cloud Clipboard)

tweaks.name: Telemetry-related scheduled tasks (selective)
tweaks.description: Disables a small allow-list of pure telemetry/compatibility tasks, one journaled task at a time, with per-task XML export and honest missing-task reporting.
tweaks.objective: Stop the classic telemetry task set without the blanket task sweeps the rejected list forbids.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxTelemetryTasks + Invoke-Nx13Rollback (src/nxcore/functions/NX13.ps1), reusing the NX11-006 mechanism pattern (allow-listed candidates only, per-task journal, no bulk sweep) and the NX16-006 baseline idea (task XML is exported before the state changes). Allow-list (TaskPath/TaskName, each with a category tag): Application Experience\Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser and Application Experience\ProgramDataUpdater (compatibility appraisal), Customer Experience Improvement Program\Consolidator, UsbCeip and KernelCeipTask (CEIP), Autochk\Proxy (app-experience inventory proxy), DiskDiagnostic\Microsoft-Windows-DiskDiagnosticDataCollector (diagnostic data collector), Feedback\Siuf\DmClient and DmClientOnScenarioDownload (feedback prompts). Explicitly EXCLUDED: WindowsUpdate\Scheduled Start, UpdateOrchestrator, maintenance/defrag tasks, Telemetry's own service, and Windows Error Reporting\QueueReporting (available only via -IncludeErrorReportingQueue with the documented trade-off that crash reports stop being queued for upload to Microsoft). Every task is probed first: a missing task is recorded as Missing with its reason and is NOT an error (the reference sets disagree by build - r5's Sophia list, r2's ReviOS/Atlas sets and r4's UltraOS safe tier all differ, and on the authoring machine build 26300.9974 the Appraiser tasks and KernelCeipTask were absent while the rest were present). Original state per task: Export-ScheduledTask XML written under <JournalRoot>\task-exports plus the pre-change State string, journaled as a 'task' target before Disable-ScheduledTask; already-disabled tasks journal a skip (AlreadyApplied). Verification re-reads Get-ScheduledTask State and journals the result. Rollback is handled by Invoke-Nx13Rollback (delegated by the core engine for 'task' targets): only-if-ours (state must still be Disabled), then Enable-ScheduledTask when the recorded original state was enabled. Boundary note for the coordinator: NX11-006 owns generic allow-listed task management - this entry owns only the telemetry allow-list above, and services are never touched (DiagTrack/WerSvc remain untouched by NEXTRIX v1). Concurrent NX11-006 cross-check (declared, not hidden): NX11-006 landed in the same wave with a broader generic allow-list that contains 8 of the 9 task names used here (Appraiser, ProgramDataUpdater, Consolidator, UsbCeip, DmClient, DmClientOnScenarioDownload, DiskDiagnosticDataCollector, Autochk Proxy) plus the WER queue and other maintenance tasks. NX13-013 therefore REUSES NX11-006's verified state changer (Set-Nx11TaskEnabled: cmdlet -> schtasks -> Task Scheduler COM, each re-read) whenever the NX11 module is loaded, and keeps its own telemetry curation, XML backup, journal attribution and rollback so an NX13 category rollback restores exactly what NX13 disabled. The two entries are idempotent against each other (whichever runs second journals AlreadyApplied and never rewrites), but the coordinator should not select both for the same task in one preset. KernelCeipTask exists only in the NX13 list and is probed, never assumed (it was absent on build 26300.9974).
tweaks.defaultState: Telemetry/compatibility tasks enabled per Windows default (some may already be absent or disabled depending on build and prior servicing).
tweaks.proposedState: Allow-listed telemetry tasks Disabled, each with an exported XML original-state artifact and a journal entry.

verify.procedure: The function re-reads each task's State via Get-ScheduledTask and journals Disabled/Unchanged per task; the result lists applied/skipped/missing tasks with reasons.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-Nx13Rollback (delegated by Invoke-NxRollback for 'task' targets) re-enables only tasks that are still Disabled and whose journaled original state was enabled; missing tasks are reported, never recreated. The exported XML is the manual restore artifact.

originalState.method: Export-ScheduledTask XML saved under <JournalRoot>\task-exports\ plus the pre-change State string, journaled as a 'task' descriptor before Disable-ScheduledTask.

sideEffects: Compatibility appraisal, CEIP uploads and feedback-prompt tasks stop running; Microsoft's diagnostic pipeline loses those inputs (this is a privacy trade-off, not a performance change).
Optional -IncludeErrorReportingQueue stops crash-report queuing for upload, reducing troubleshooting data available to Microsoft and to per-app crash flows.
Task sets differ by build: absent tasks are reported as Missing, not treated as applied.

NX11-006 overlaps 8 of the 9 task names; both entries are idempotent against each other, but selecting both for the same task is redundant (see technicalExplanation) and NX13 remains the owner of the telemetry selection.
documentationSource: r5-winutil-sophia.md (ScheduledTasks allow-list pattern: MareBackup, Compatibility Appraiser, StartupAppTask, Proxy, Consolidator, UsbCeip, DiskDiagnosticDataCollector)
r4-synergy-ultraos.md (telemetry-tasks.yml safe tier with ignoreErrors because Win10-era tasks no longer exist on Win11)
r2-atlasos-revios.md (FINALIZE.cmd task list; Atlas NoTelemetry component inventory)
registry/NX11.json NX11-006 (mechanism owner for generic selective task management; Set-Nx11TaskEnabled reused)

tweaks.name: Permission audit report
tweaks.description: Read-only privacy posture report: app-permission policy and consent-store state, diagnostics level with edition floor, and the state of every switch this category manages.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner (and the Privacy-Focused profile P8) an evidence-based picture of the machine's privacy configuration before deciding anything.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxPrivacyAuditReport (src/nxcore/functions/NX13.ps1): read-only, never journals, never mutates. It reports, with explicit uncertainty instead of guesses: (1) per-capability picture for location/camera/microphone/contacts/calendar - the AppPrivacy policy value (0/1/2 or absent), the current-user consent-store top-level value (HKCU\...\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\<capability>\Value, string Allow/Deny) and per-app Allow/Deny counts, mapping camera->'webcam' and calendar->'appointments' (the OS consent-store names, verified read-only on build 26300); (2) diagnostic data: AllowTelemetry value, the resolved edition floor from NX13-004's resolver, whether the floor is documented-only-for-this-edition, and the dump/log limit values; (3) every switch this category writes - advertising ID, activity feed trio, tailored experiences, app-launch tracking policy, General toggles, feedback frequency pair, inking/typing restrict pair, cloud search pair, clipboard history, cross-device (EnableMmx/AllowCrossDeviceClipboard) - reported as configured / not-configured / wrong-kind (UnsupportedValue) without changing anything; (4) the telemetry task allow-list state (Disabled/Ready/Missing) read-only. The report answers 'what is configured', not 'is it better' - no performance claim is made anywhere (directive). P8 consumption: the result is a plain PowerShell object with stable property names (findings[] with area/target/kind/value/meaning, plus uncertainty[]) so the profile layer can render it directly.
tweaks.proposedState: Machine-readable + human-readable privacy posture report available on demand.

verify.procedure: The report object has readOnly=true, a non-empty findings array, and an uncertainty array listing every value that could not be read (missing key, kind mismatch, cmdlet unavailable).

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic; nothing is journaled because nothing is changed.

originalState.method: Not applicable - the report IS the current-state artifact.

sideEffects: None (read-only registry/CIM reads; per-app consent-store enumeration is bounded).
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/manage-connections-from-windows-operating-system-components-to-microsoft-services (18.x Settings > Privacy reference values used by the report map)
